subject: Urgent: Skyline Health p95 spike on skyline-v2.1 — request for rollback / SLA concession
messages:
From: Skyline Health Ops <ops@skyline.health>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: latency alert — skyline-v2.1 p95 jump since 18:00 UTC (request IDs & traces attached)

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing a large P95 jump on requests routed to model skyline-v2.1 yesterday ~18:00 UTC. Baseline p95 for our chat endpoint was ~180ms; since the promotion it sits at ~580ms for many production requests and a noticeable increase in user timeouts. We attached sample request IDs and a short traces CSV.

Impact: degraded UX on several high-frequency flows (search + compose). We’re seeing batching stalls and increased tail latency across short and long contexts. Our QA is blocked on the increased TTFB.

Can Redwood either: 1) rollback traffic to skyline-v2.0, or 2) authorize a temporary SLA concession while you investigate? We need an answer within the next 4 hours so we can decide whether to divert traffic client-side.

Attached: skyline_perfcounters_20250518.csv, sample_request_ids.txt

— A. Patel
Ops Lead, Skyline Health

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: ops@skyline.health; ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-18T09:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: latency alert — skyline-v2.1 p95 jump since 18:00 UTC (request IDs & traces attached)

Thanks for flagging — and sorry for the disruption, A.

Ben, can you triage access patterns and confirm whether the v2.1 rollout caused any memory/KV-cache shifts? Monica, please prepare a short customer update and list acceptable remediation options (rollback vs traffic fencing vs temporary SLO leniency).

We should treat this as a provisional SLA exception request if we need more than a hotfix window. Ben, if rollback is safe, include the expected customer impact and time to complete. Need a recommendation in the next 60–90 minutes.

— Lauren
Head of Customer Reliability (on-call)

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-18T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: latency alert — skyline-v2.1 p95 jump since 18:00 UTC (request IDs & traces attached)

On Sun, May 18, 2025 at 9:29 AM lauren.bishop@redwood.ai wrote:
> Ben, can you triage access patterns and confirm whether the v2.1 rollout caused any memory/KV-cache shifts?

Quick triage summary:
- Root cause hypothesis: a configuration change in the v2.1 variant (KV cache key namespace update + slightly larger embedding table) caused an elevated cache miss rate under Skyline's traffic shape. Misses lead to extra CPU+device transfers and sporadic batching stalls.
- Evidence: canary_telemetry_snapshot.json attached (span-level p95, cache hit/miss rates). Metric delta lines up with the deployment timestamp.
- Options: 1) Immediate rollback to skyline-v2.0 (estimated 7–12 minute safe rollback window, brief request queuing during switch). 2) Traffic fencing: shift 80% -> v2.0, 20% -> v2.1 to monitor (safe, slower impact). 3) Temporary SLO concession (we can grant a 48–72h grace window) while we push a variant patch addressing the cache namespace.

Recommendation: authorize an automatic rollback to v2.0 now. If leadership approves, I’ll kick off the rollback and monitor tail latencies; we’ll keep a canary slice on v2.1 for regression verification.

Attachments: canary_telemetry_snapshot.json (perf counters), rollback_playbook.md (internal)

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-18T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: RE: latency alert — customer comms + SLA amendment draft

Lauren / Ben —

If we proceed with rollback, suggested customer-facing messaging (short):
- Acknowledge: "We're seeing elevated tail latency on skyline-v2.1; we are rolling traffic back to skyline-v2.0 to restore SLOs immediately."
- ETA: "We expect routing stabilization within ~15 minutes of the rollback completing; we will monitor for 48 hours and share a post-mortem."
- Concession ask: propose a 48-hour provisional grace window (no SLA credit) and offer a 2% usage credit if issues persist beyond 48 hours; if customer insists we can offer a drafted DocuSign amendment for a 72-hour formal grace with a small credit.

I attached a draft SLA amendment (docusign_sla_amendment_draft.pdf) we can send if Skyline requires a written concession. Also included suggested copy for the support ticket and a scheduled check-in with the customer at +24h.

— Monica
Customer Success Manager

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: ops@skyline.health, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-18T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Decision: rollback + provisional SLA exception (48h) — next steps

Hi A. / Skyline Ops —

We've authorized an immediate rollback to skyline-v2.0. Ben will execute the rollback and monitor tail latency for the next 2 hours. Operations will keep a minimal canary on v2.1 for regression verification.

We are also granting a provisional SLA concession window of 48 hours to allow time for a patch and verification; this is conditional on:
- A full post-mortem delivered within 72 hours that identifies root cause and remediation plan;
- No repeat degradation on v2.0 within the 48-hour window;
- Agreement on any formal amendment if Skyline requests an official contract change (Monica has the DocuSign draft ready).

Ben: proceed with rollback now. Monica: send the below short note to the ops ticket and offer the 48h provisional window; escalate DocuSign only if the customer requests a formal amendment.

Apologies again for the interruption — we’ll follow up with telemetry and the post-mortem.

— Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachments sent: skyline_perfcounters_20250518.csv; canary_telemetry_snapshot.json; docusign_sla_amendment_draft.pdf
